Built on vanilla JavaScript and the reactive model of Observable Notebook Kit, Recho Notebook lets developers, artists, and learners explore algorithms and ASCII art interactively.

embeddings.title: Power & Ground
embeddings.description:
My thesis project is my own answer to the question, What will happen to the music? what happens when we rely on western and colonial structures for our sound and signal? 

Our sounds are limited by our hardware. What happens when the systems don’t want to listen to your music? when they encourage specific sounds? How does that change how your body moves through space? Why in 2026 would a system want to control the movement of your body?

embeddings.title: no no ordinary - the shape of things unseen
embeddings.description: The piece translates any visible scene or image into the way I perceive it internally with Aphantasia. This project is for people who rely on sight as their primary way of understanding the world, as well as those who do not experience visual imagination in the same way. It is meant for anyone curious about how differently our minds build images, whether they picture scenes clearly, vaguely, or not at all.

embeddings.title: Odyssey
embeddings.description: Odyssey is a video-based interactive storytelling experience that constructs cinema as a navigable space using machine learning. It comprises of a physical interface, a machine learning system, and a collection of footage filmed using a DV camcorder. Instead of watching the story in a linear way, Odyssey invites audiences to input words and phrases to assemble timelines using these footage, which they will then traverse through by tuning the interface to understand the story.

embeddings.title: AFTER 10 DAYS, BALANCE IS RESTORED.
embeddings.description:
"After 10 days, balance is restored" is a time-based kinetic sculpture made with living cut sunflowers. Before installation, the flowers are weighed to ensure they are equal, and the structure begins in balance.

As days pass, because each flower is an individual — with its own biological timeline and metabolism — one always dies faster, losing body weight more quickly. This creates an imbalance that shifts the water distribution: the heavier side receives more water, while the lighter side is left with fewer resources and a greater risk of air entering its xylem, disrupting the continuity of water flow within the stem. The imbalance deepens because of this.
But after 10 days, the balance is restored. Because after 10 days, both sunflowers are equally dead — neither can absorb water anymore. In fact, both have lost so much body weight that they can no longer form a seal between the hose and the clamp, and the water simply leaks out.

All imbalance, all striving, competing, struggling — eventually, balance is restored.

The three pairs of flowers in the installation are arranged left to right: freshly installed (balanced) in the center, installed five days prior (unbalanced) on the left, and installed more than ten days ago (balanced again) on the right.

embeddings.title: THE SHEEPLE'S COURT
embeddings.description:
Don't care what others think of you? You sure?

What’s it feel like when someone sums you up in one sound? A flippant grunt - or maybe they applaud you? How do you respond - internally?

Much of our lives center around gaining respect. But how much of that is earning self-respect, and how much is feeling respected in the eyes of others? What happens to your sense of self worth when you’re randomly and unfairly judged? Running the Gauntlet through “THE SHEEPLE’S COURT” will help you answer that question.  

The purpose of this installation is both social and psychological. It’s designed to build personal awareness of how social judgement shapes our sense of self, while providing a humorous interactive experience.

embeddings.title: Attention & Effort
embeddings.description:
The dominant narrative around AI is speed and throughput. Attention & Effort argues the opposite: a tool's value is partly measured by how much room it leaves for the user. Room to look closely. Room to keep working.

The presentation focuses on two prototypes that work this question through image generation. Drawing & Speaking treats attention as the primary input: you draw on top of an image and speak about your changes, and the model edits along the trace you left. The closer you look, the more accurately it moves you toward what you actually want.

Training AI to Paint with Code shifts engagement to the model itself: instead of generating images directly, an LLM writes p5.brush code that renders the image, leaving a recipe you can read, modify, and inherit. We then train the model further with reinforcement learning to paint better.

Together they ask where, in our use of this technology, dignity is preserved. Where we are still asked to look closely and to participate in the work.

embeddings.description:

Selected Recording Transcripts of Life Data Recorder Prototype (MRU-0)

The Life Data Recorder Prototype (MRU-0) was developed in █████ by a joint team from █████. Its stated purpose was to function as a data visualization device for life data research, capturing subjects’ real-time physiological and affective responses to generate analytical reports for clinical use.

Following a limited phase of internal testing, the project was terminated by its host institution. No units were produced beyond the prototype stage, and all early prototypes and developmental versions were destroyed. No public explanation was provided. Technology media widely attributed the termination to insufficient return on investment and a lack of viable commercial applications, describing it as “a failed commercial experiment.”

After the project’s termination, the lead researcher, ████████ (hereafter referred to as “the donor”), left the institution and retained the surviving prototype, MRU-0, for continued independent interviews. During this period, multiple attempts by private technology collectors to acquire the device were declined.

Prior to their passing, the donor bequeathed MRU-0, along with its complete archive of recordings and related documents, to this museum. No additional written explanation was left. The recordings presented in this exhibition are drawn from the original MRU-0 archive and have been restored and prepared by the curatorial team.

In accordance with the donor’s wishes, all identities and sensitive information have been anonymized.

embeddings.title: Placement
embeddings.description:
Commercial cinema has long operated as a dual medium: a vehicle for narrative and, simultaneously, a platform for brand communication. Product placement—the contractual embedding of logos, products, and corporate identities within the mise-en-scène—functions through studied inconspicuousness, relying on the viewer's absorption in story to render commerce invisible and subliminal. 
                                                                
Placement isolates and foregrounds this secondary register.
                                                                                
Employing a custom computer vision pipeline trained on object detection, the piece systematically scans a feature film frame by frame, identifying and extracting every instance of brand presence. The source footage is discarded. What remains is an uninterrupted cropped and sequenced stream composed entirely of product placements.

Severed from narrative context, these fragments take on an unsettling quality. Logos drift through frameless space; audio exists only in the context of brand presence; corporate insignia recur with the rhythm of a pattern rather than the logic of a scene. 

In doing so, Placement positions itself within a lineage of appropriation and re-contextualization, from the found-footage traditions of structural film to contemporary practices of database cinema, while directing its attention toward the specific economy of attention that underwrites commercial moviemaking.
